chapter: Washington clubs, Louis Jordan and Sarah Vaughan, 1949-54
title: Bassist Israel Crosby, the legend he most enjoyed working with
summary: A quiet, unassuming bass legend who had played with Fletcher Henderson, Crosby joins Sarah's first trio.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: But when we got into Chicago, Sarah made arrangements to have a trio. She knew a couple of fellows in Chicago, a bass player who I had heard about since the late Thirties, who was a legend among bass players. The first I heard about him was when he was working with Fletcher Henderson, and from what I understand, he was a teenager at that particular. But this fellow's name was Israel Crosby. Which I have worked with a lot of bass players... I have worked with a lot of bass players before and since, and I have never worked with any bass player that I enjoyed working with any more than Israel Crosby.

Too much can't be said about Israel Crosby as a musician and a bass player. The only thing about it is, he was a quiet, unassuming person that... All of the musicians knew what a great bass player he was. And bass players, off course, certainly knew. But he was around during the Jimmy Blanton fame, and the fame of a lot of other bass players,
Oscar Pettiford and all of them. But Israel Crosby was the kind of guy that, if you didn't know it, you'd never hear from him that he was even a musician,
